validation.note: Generated structured draft records; numeric-entry and complex-format keys require clinical/editorial completion before production exam use.

items.title: An older adult with stable dementia becomes acutely inattentive and disoriented over 12 hours. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Assess for delirium triggers including infection, hypoxia, pain, medications, and dehydration; provide orientation and safety measures.
items.rationale: Acute fluctuating change is delirium until evaluated, not expected dementia progression.

items.title: A client says, “My diagnosis means my life is over.” The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Use an open-ended response such as, “What worries you most about the diagnosis?” and explore feelings without false reassurance.
items.rationale: Open-ended reflection encourages expression and assessment of the client's concerns.

items.title: A client with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted with cough, night sweats, and weight loss. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Place in airborne infection isolation, use fit-tested respirator, and obtain sputum specimens as ordered.
items.rationale: Pulmonary TB spreads via airborne particles and requires airborne precautions.

items.title: A nurse sustains a hollow-bore needlestick after blood exposure. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A nurse sustains a hollow-bore needlestick after blood exposure.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Wash area, report immediately, document exposure, and obtain urgent occupational-health assessment for HIV/HBV/HCV postexposure management.
items.rationale: Time-sensitive risk assessment and prophylaxis reduce transmission risk.

items.title: An outdoor worker is confused with core temperature 40.5°C and hot skin. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:An outdoor worker is confused with core temperature 40.5°C and hot skin.|response:Activate emergency response and begin rapid active cooling while supporting airway/circulation; do not delay cooling for antipyretics.|rationale:Heat stroke is thermoregulatory failure; rapid cooling is lifesaving and antipyretics are ineffective.
items.rationale: Heat stroke is thermoregulatory failure; rapid cooling is lifesaving and antipyretics are ineffective.

items.title: Several household members have headache and nausea after a faulty heater; pulse oximetry reads 99%. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Carbon monoxide poisoning|priority:Remove from exposure, administer high-concentration oxygen, obtain carboxyhemoglobin testing, and evaluate for hyperbaric therapy when indicated.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Standard pulse oximetry may appear normal because it cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin.

items.title: A client with hypertension and atrial fibrillation asks how to reduce stroke risk. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Stroke prevention teaching|actions:Reinforce BP control, prescribed anticoagulation adherence, smoking cessation, and urgent response to FAST symptoms.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Atrial fibrillation and hypertension are modifiable stroke risks; anticoagulation reduces embolic stroke risk when indicated.

items.title: A severely immunocompromised client asks about receiving a live attenuated vaccine. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A severely immunocompromised client asks about receiving a live attenuated vaccine.|priority:Verify immune status and vaccine-specific guidance; defer live vaccine when contraindicated and consult immunization provider.
items.rationale: Live vaccines may cause disease in severe immunosuppression; decisions depend on the specific condition and vaccine.

items.title: After a mass-casualty event, a walking client has minor abrasions while another is apneic. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Disaster triage prioritizes greatest survivable benefit with limited resources; follow local START/JumpSTART protocol.

items.title: An immobile older adult has intact skin with nonblanchable erythema over the sacrum. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Nonblanchable erythema indicates a stage 1 pressure injury; pressure relief prevents progression.

items.title: An older adult with orthostatic hypotension fell while walking to the bathroom at night. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Assess injury and orthostatic vitals, review medications, provide assisted toileting and environmental modifications, and use individualized fall precautions.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Addressing orthostasis and environmental hazards reduces recurrent falls.

items.title: A new ileostomy appears dusky purple and has stopped producing output with increasing abdominal pain. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Notify surgeon urgently and assess perfusion/obstruction; a healthy stoma should be moist and pink to red.
items.rationale: Dusky discoloration suggests ischemia; absent output with pain may indicate obstruction.

items.title: A client with an AV fistula has no palpable thrill or audible bruit. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Dialysis access|actions:Do not use the access; notify dialysis team immediately and assess distal circulation.|evaluation:Absent thrill/bruit suggests thrombosis or access failure requiring urgent evaluation.
items.rationale: Absent thrill/bruit suggests thrombosis or access failure requiring urgent evaluation.

items.title: A client on peritoneal dialysis reports abdominal pain and cloudy effluent. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Collect effluent specimen as prescribed, notify dialysis team, and prepare for prompt intraperitoneal antibiotics.
items.rationale: Cloudy effluent and abdominal pain are classic signs of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis.

items.title: A client using home oxygen asks whether smoking near an open window is safe. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Explain that smoking is prohibited near oxygen; keep oxygen away from flames/heat and post no-smoking signage.
items.rationale: Oxygen accelerates combustion and creates severe fire risk.

items.title: A client with advanced illness has distressing dyspnea despite oxygen saturation 93%. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Assess distress and reversible causes, use positioning/fan and prescribed opioid for air hunger, and align care with goals.
items.rationale: Dyspnea is subjective; opioids can relieve air hunger even when oxygen saturation is not severely low.

items.title: A competent client with a valid advance directive refuses a proposed treatment; family demands it. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A competent client with a valid advance directive refuses a proposed treatment; family demands it.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Respect the client's informed decision, clarify goals, notify care team, and document discussion.
items.rationale: A competent adult's informed choices guide care; family preference does not override autonomy.

items.title: A client scheduled for surgery says they do not understand the procedure after the surgeon left. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A client scheduled for surgery says they do not understand the procedure after the surgeon left.|response:Pause preparation and contact the surgeon to provide further explanation; the nurse witnesses consent and assesses voluntariness/understanding.|rationale:The procedural provider is responsible for explaining risks, benefits, and alternatives; consent must be informed.
items.rationale: The procedural provider is responsible for explaining risks, benefits, and alternatives; consent must be informed.

items.title: A stable client needs routine vital signs while another client has new chest pain. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Delegation|priority:Delegate routine vital signs for the stable client to qualified assistive personnel and personally assess the client with chest pain.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Unstable/new symptoms require RN assessment; predictable tasks for stable clients may be delegated with follow-up.

items.title: A confused client repeatedly attempts to climb out of bed; family asks for restraints. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Restraint safety|actions:Assess causes and use least-restrictive alternatives first; if restraint is necessary, follow order, monitoring, release, and documentation requirements.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Restraints are last resort and require ongoing assessment and legal/policy safeguards.

items.title: A nurse discovers that a client received twice the prescribed insulin dose. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A nurse discovers that a client received twice the prescribed insulin dose.|priority:Assess glucose and symptoms immediately, notify provider, initiate hypoglycemia monitoring/treatment, and report per policy.
items.rationale: Patient assessment and prevention of harm take priority over blame; insulin overdose can cause delayed hypoglycemia.

items.title: A caller claiming to be a client's employer asks for the client's diagnosis. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Health information may be shared only with authorized persons and for permitted purposes.

items.title: A conscious client with diabetes is diaphoretic and has glucose 48 mg/dL. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: The 15-15 approach treats an alert client able to swallow; altered consciousness requires glucagon/IV dextrose.

items.title: A chronic wound has purulent drainage, spreading erythema, fever, and increasing pain. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Assess for systemic infection, obtain ordered cultures, notify provider promptly, and provide wound care/antimicrobials as prescribed.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Local wound deterioration with fever may indicate spreading infection or sepsis.

items.title: A client with a central venous catheter develops rigors during infusion and fever. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Stop infusion if clinically indicated, assess stability, notify provider, obtain paired cultures as ordered, and follow line infection protocol.
items.rationale: Rigors during infusion raise concern for bloodstream infection and require prompt evaluation.

items.title: A client with sodium 118 mEq/L develops headache, confusion, and a seizure. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Electrolyte imbalance—hyponatremia|actions:Protect airway and safety, notify emergency team, and anticipate carefully controlled hypertonic saline when indicated with frequent sodium checks.|evaluation:Severe symptomatic hyponatremia causes cerebral edema; correction must be controlled to avoid osmotic demyelination.
items.rationale: Severe symptomatic hyponatremia causes cerebral edema; correction must be controlled to avoid osmotic demyelination.

items.title: A client with malignancy has calcium 14.2 mg/dL, constipation, weakness, and confusion. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Initiate prescribed isotonic IV hydration, monitor ECG/renal function, and prepare ordered calcium-lowering therapy.
items.rationale: Severe hypercalcemia causes neurologic, renal, and cardiac effects; hydration supports renal calcium excretion.

items.title: After thyroidectomy, a client reports perioral tingling and has carpopedal spasm. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Assess airway and calcium, notify provider, and prepare IV calcium gluconate for symptomatic hypocalcemia.
items.rationale: Parathyroid injury can cause acute hypocalcemia and tetany; laryngospasm is a serious risk.

items.title: A client with untreated hyperthyroidism has fever 40°C, HR 160/min, agitation, and diarrhea. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Activate emergency response, provide cooling and cardiac monitoring, and administer prescribed beta blocker, antithyroid medication, and supportive therapy.
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is life-threatening thyrotoxicosis with hyperthermia and cardiovascular instability.

items.title: An older adult with hypothyroidism is hypothermic, bradycardic, hypotensive, and obtunded. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:An older adult with hypothyroidism is hypothermic, bradycardic, hypotensive, and obtunded.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Support airway/ventilation and circulation, initiate emergency care, and anticipate IV thyroid hormone and cautious warming as prescribed.
items.rationale: Severe hypothyroidism can cause life-threatening hypometabolism and respiratory/circulatory failure.

items.title: A client with Addison disease has vomiting, abdominal pain, BP 76/42 mm Hg, sodium 126, and potassium 6.0. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A client with Addison disease has vomiting, abdominal pain, BP 76/42 mm Hg, sodium 126, and potassium 6.0.|response:Escalate immediately, administer prescribed IV hydrocortisone and isotonic fluids, and monitor glucose/electrolytes.|rationale:Adrenal crisis causes shock and electrolyte disturbance; prompt steroid and fluid replacement are essential.
items.rationale: Adrenal crisis causes shock and electrolyte disturbance; prompt steroid and fluid replacement are essential.

items.title: A client with small-cell lung cancer has sodium 122 mEq/L, low serum osmolality, and concentrated urine. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:SIADH|priority:Institute prescribed fluid restriction, monitor neurologic status and sodium, and use hypertonic saline only for severe symptoms as ordered.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Excess ADH causes water retention and dilutional hyponatremia; correction requires close monitoring.

items.title: A client with peripheral neuropathy has a painless blister under the forefoot. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Diabetes foot care|actions:Inspect feet daily, avoid self-treatment of lesions, use properly fitted footwear, and arrange prompt foot-care evaluation.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Neuropathy masks injury; early evaluation prevents ulceration and infection.

items.title: A client taking methotrexate reports fever and mouth ulcers. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A client taking methotrexate reports fever and mouth ulcers.|priority:Hold dose pending urgent prescriber review, obtain CBC/liver/renal assessment as ordered, and screen for infection/toxicity.
items.rationale: Methotrexate can cause myelosuppression and mucositis; fever may indicate serious infection.

items.title: A client with lupus has new edema, hypertension, proteinuria, and rising creatinine. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Proteinuria and renal impairment suggest organ involvement requiring prompt treatment.

items.title: An older adult taking long-term glucocorticoids has low bone density. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Glucocorticoids increase fracture risk; multifactorial prevention is required.

items.title: A client with Parkinson disease coughs during meals and has a wet voice afterward. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Stop oral intake pending swallow evaluation, position upright, use prescribed texture modifications, and provide oral care.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Cough and wet voice suggest aspiration; swallowing assessment guides safe nutrition.

items.title: A client with myasthenia gravis develops weak cough, dysphagia, and declining vital capacity. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Escalate to critical care, assess respiratory mechanics and airway protection, and prepare ventilatory support.
items.rationale: Bulbar and respiratory muscle weakness can progress to respiratory failure.

items.title: A client has ascending weakness and declining forced vital capacity after a respiratory infection. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Guillain-Barré syndrome|actions:Notify critical care team, monitor respiratory function and autonomic instability, and prepare for ventilatory support and IVIG/plasma exchange.|evaluation:Respiratory failure and dysautonomia are major threats in Guillain-Barré syndrome.
items.rationale: Respiratory failure and dysautonomia are major threats in Guillain-Barré syndrome.

items.title: A client with MS reports transient worsening of weakness after a hot shower. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Recommend cooling strategies, avoiding overheating, pacing activity, and reporting new persistent neurologic deficits.
items.rationale: Heat can temporarily worsen conduction in demyelinated nerves; persistent changes require evaluation.

items.title: A client rescued from an enclosed fire has facial burns, soot in sputum, and hoarseness. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Activate airway response early, administer high-concentration oxygen, and prepare for early intubation assessment.
items.rationale: Airway edema can progress rapidly after inhalation injury; early airway control may be necessary.

items.title: A client has small entry and exit burns after high-voltage exposure and reports palpitations. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Ensure scene safety, obtain ECG and cardiac monitoring, assess deep tissue injury and rhabdomyolysis, and arrange urgent evaluation.
items.rationale: External burns underestimate deep injury; dysrhythmias and muscle damage may occur.

items.title: An older adult found outdoors has core temperature 32°C, confusion, and shivering. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:An older adult found outdoors has core temperature 32°C, confusion, and shivering.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Handle gently, remove wet clothing, initiate controlled rewarming, monitor cardiac rhythm, and avoid rough movement.
items.rationale: Moderate hypothermia can cause dysrhythmias; gentle handling and controlled rewarming reduce risk.

items.title: A rescued swimmer is coughing, hypoxemic, and has crackles despite being awake. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A rescued swimmer is coughing, hypoxemic, and has crackles despite being awake.|response:Support oxygenation and ventilation, monitor for pulmonary edema, and arrange emergency evaluation and observation.|rationale:Respiratory complications may evolve after submersion even when the client is initially alert.
items.rationale: Respiratory complications may evolve after submersion even when the client is initially alert.

items.title: A client presents after a suspected venomous snakebite with progressive swelling and pain. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Snakebite|priority:Keep client calm and limb immobilized at heart level, remove constricting items, mark swelling, and contact poison control/prepare antivenom assessment.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Avoid tourniquets, cutting, suction, or ice; serial assessment guides antivenom need.

items.title: A child may have swallowed household drain cleaner and is drooling. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Poisoning—caustic ingestion|actions:Do not induce vomiting or attempt neutralization; protect airway and contact poison control/emergency services immediately.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Caustic agents cause further injury if vomited or chemically neutralized; airway and specialist guidance are priorities.

items.title: A farm worker has miosis, salivation, bronchorrhea, bradycardia, and muscle fasciculations. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A farm worker has miosis, salivation, bronchorrhea, bradycardia, and muscle fasciculations.|priority:Use appropriate PPE/decontamination, support airway, and prepare atropine and pralidoxime per protocol.
items.rationale: Cholinergic excess causes life-threatening bronchorrhea and bradycardia; protect rescuers from secondary exposure.

items.title: A toddler may have ingested multiple iron tablets and now has vomiting and abdominal pain. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Iron poisoning can cause severe GI injury, shock, and metabolic toxicity; early specialist treatment matters.

items.title: A client has tinnitus, tachypnea, vomiting, and mixed respiratory alkalosis/metabolic acidosis after overdose. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Salicylate toxicity causes characteristic tinnitus and mixed acid-base disturbance; serum levels and pH guide care.

items.title: A runner has heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea, and temperature 38.2°C but remains oriented. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Move to cool area, remove excess clothing, provide oral fluids if alert, cool externally, and monitor for progression.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Heat exhaustion usually preserves mental status; altered mentation or very high core temperature suggests heat stroke.

items.title: A client with heart failure gains 2.5 kg in 3 days and reports increasing orthopnea. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Notify provider promptly, assess congestion and oxygenation, review diuretic plan, and reinforce daily weights and symptom action plan.
items.rationale: Rapid weight gain and orthopnea suggest fluid retention and worsening heart failure.

items.title: A client reports sudden tearing chest/back pain with unequal arm blood pressures. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Aortic dissection|actions:Activate emergency response, minimize exertion, monitor hemodynamics, and prepare prescribed IV beta blockade and urgent imaging.|evaluation:Aortic dissection is a vascular emergency; reducing shear stress and rapid diagnosis are essential.
items.rationale: Aortic dissection is a vascular emergency; reducing shear stress and rapid diagnosis are essential.

items.title: A client after cardiac surgery has hypotension, jugular venous distention, muffled heart sounds, and narrowing pulse pressure. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Escalate immediately, support oxygenation and circulation, and prepare for urgent echocardiography/pericardial drainage.
items.rationale: Beck triad and hemodynamic compromise suggest tamponade obstructing cardiac filling.

items.title: A client has irregular HR 158/min, BP 118/72 mm Hg, and palpitations without chest pain or syncope. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Assess stability, obtain ECG, notify provider, and prepare rate-control/anticoagulation decisions based on clinical context.
items.rationale: Stable AF with rapid ventricular response requires ECG confirmation and individualized rate/rhythm and stroke-risk management.

items.title: A monitored client becomes unresponsive, pulseless, and the rhythm is ventricular fibrillation. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Start CPR and defibrillate as soon as possible; follow ACLS and minimize interruptions.
items.rationale: VF is a shockable cardiac-arrest rhythm; early defibrillation and high-quality CPR improve survival.

items.title: A client has HR 34/min, BP 78/42 mm Hg, chest discomfort, and altered mentation. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A client has HR 34/min, BP 78/42 mm Hg, chest discomfort, and altered mentation.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Activate emergency response, support airway/circulation, prepare atropine and transcutaneous pacing per ACLS.
items.rationale: Bradycardia with hypotension and altered mentation is unstable and requires immediate intervention.

items.title: On postoperative day 1, a client has low-grade fever, diminished bases, and shallow respirations. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:On postoperative day 1, a client has low-grade fever, diminished bases, and shallow respirations.|response:Encourage early ambulation, upright positioning, deep breathing and incentive spirometry, and adequate analgesia.|rationale:Pain-related shallow breathing and immobility promote atelectasis; lung expansion and mobility help prevent it.
items.rationale: Pain-related shallow breathing and immobility promote atelectasis; lung expansion and mobility help prevent it.

items.title: A client taking rifampin notices orange discoloration of urine and tears. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Pulmonary tuberculosis medication|priority:Explain that orange-red body-fluid discoloration is expected, reinforce adherence, and review hepatotoxicity and drug interactions.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Rifampin commonly discolors body fluids; adherence and liver monitoring remain important.

items.title: A client has frequent watery diarrhea after antibiotics and a positive C. difficile test. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:C. difficile infection|actions:Initiate contact precautions with soap-and-water hand hygiene, use sporicidal environmental cleaning, and administer prescribed therapy.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: C. difficile spores resist alcohol hand rub; contact precautions and soap-and-water reduce spread.

items.title: A hospitalized client has confirmed influenza with cough and fever. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A hospitalized client has confirmed influenza with cough and fever.|priority:Use droplet precautions, appropriate mask and eye protection per policy, and encourage respiratory hygiene.
items.rationale: Influenza primarily spreads by respiratory droplets; follow facility-specific infection-control guidance.

items.title: A client 5 days after surgery has wound separation, purulent drainage, and fever. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Dehiscence/evisceration risk requires protection and urgent surgical evaluation.

items.title: A postoperative abdominal incision opens and bowel is visible. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Do not attempt to replace organs; moist sterile protection and urgent surgical care are essential.

items.title: Two hours after thyroidectomy, a client develops stridor and neck swelling. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Call emergency response, assess airway, apply oxygen, and prepare for immediate airway intervention.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Neck hematoma or laryngeal edema can rapidly obstruct the airway.

items.title: A client on postoperative day 3 has unilateral calf swelling, warmth, and tenderness. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Notify provider for urgent evaluation, avoid massaging the leg, and anticipate diagnostic ultrasound and anticoagulation if confirmed.
items.rationale: Unilateral swelling suggests DVT; massage may dislodge thrombus.

items.title: A client after hip replacement is reluctant to use sequential compression devices. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Pulmonary embolism prevention|actions:Explain purpose, apply devices correctly when in bed, encourage early ambulation, and administer prescribed prophylaxis.|evaluation:Mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis reduce postoperative venous thromboembolism risk.
items.rationale: Mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis reduce postoperative venous thromboembolism risk.

items.title: A client with iron-deficiency anemia reports fatigue and has microcytic indices and low ferritin. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Administer prescribed iron, teach absorption strategies and expected dark stools/constipation, and investigate source of iron loss.
items.rationale: Low ferritin and microcytosis support iron deficiency; replacement and cause evaluation are needed.

items.title: A client with sickle cell disease has severe back and leg pain without fever or respiratory symptoms. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Assess pain and complications, provide prompt prescribed analgesia and hydration, and encourage incentive spirometry when appropriate.
items.rationale: Vaso-occlusive crisis requires timely analgesia and prevention of dehydration and acute chest syndrome.

items.title: A client with transfusion-dependent thalassemia receives regular packed RBCs and has elevated ferritin. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Monitor transfusion reactions and iron burden, reinforce chelation adherence, and trend cardiac/hepatic iron assessment.
items.rationale: Repeated transfusions cause iron overload; chelation prevents organ damage.

items.title: A child with hemophilia A has painful swollen knee after minor trauma. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A child with hemophilia A has painful swollen knee after minor trauma.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Administer prescribed factor VIII promptly, rest/ice/elevate joint, and avoid IM injections and aspirin/NSAIDs unless specifically directed.
items.rationale: Early factor replacement prevents hemarthrosis-related joint damage.

items.title: A client with ANC 400 asks whether fresh flowers can be kept in the room. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A client with ANC 400 asks whether fresh flowers can be kept in the room.|response:Follow facility protective-environment policy, avoid standing water/soil exposure, perform hand hygiene, and report fever immediately.|rationale:Soil and standing water can harbor organisms; neutropenic fever requires urgent action.
items.rationale: Soil and standing water can harbor organisms; neutropenic fever requires urgent action.

items.title: A client with platelets 18,000/mm³ has petechiae and gingival bleeding. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Thrombocytopenia bleeding|priority:Institute bleeding precautions, avoid IM/rectal procedures and NSAIDs, use soft oral care, and report active bleeding.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Severe thrombocytopenia increases spontaneous bleeding risk; minimize trauma.

items.title: A septic client oozes from IV sites, has platelets 42,000/mm³, prolonged PT, and low fibrinogen. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Disseminated intravascular coagulation|actions:Treat underlying cause urgently, monitor bleeding/thrombosis and labs, and prepare blood component support as prescribed.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: DIC consumes platelets and clotting factors while causing microthrombi and bleeding.

items.title: During transfusion, an older client develops dyspnea, hypertension, crackles, and jugular venous distention. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:During transfusion, an older client develops dyspnea, hypertension, crackles, and jugular venous distention.|priority:Stop transfusion, sit upright, provide oxygen, notify provider/blood bank, and anticipate diuretic treatment.
items.rationale: TACO is volume overload; respiratory support and diuresis are often required.

items.title: Within 2 hours of transfusion, a client develops acute hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, and hypotension without fluid overload. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: TRALI causes noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and requires supportive care; diuretics are not routine absent overload.

items.title: A postpartum client reports hearing voices telling her to harm the infant. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Postpartum psychosis is an emergency with risk of harm and requires immediate protection and treatment.

items.title: A client 3 weeks postpartum reports persistent sadness, guilt, and inability to enjoy usual activities but denies intent to self-harm. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Assess suicide and infant-safety risk directly, use validated screening, and arrange prompt mental-health support.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Persistent symptoms beyond transient blues warrant assessment and treatment; safety questions are essential.

items.title: A 36-hour-old newborn has jaundice extending to the abdomen and poor feeding. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Obtain age-in-hours bilirubin assessment, evaluate feeding/hydration and hemolysis risk, and initiate phototherapy if threshold met.
items.rationale: Bilirubin treatment thresholds depend on age in hours and risk factors; early assessment prevents neurotoxicity.

items.title: A 2-day-old newborn has temperature instability, poor feeding, lethargy, and apnea. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Newborn sepsis|actions:Escalate urgently, support airway/temperature/glucose, obtain cultures as ordered, and initiate prescribed empiric antibiotics promptly.|evaluation:Neonatal infection may present subtly and progress rapidly; prompt stabilization and treatment are vital.
items.rationale: Neonatal infection may present subtly and progress rapidly; prompt stabilization and treatment are vital.

items.title: A caregiver plans to place a newborn prone on a soft pillow for sleep. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Teach supine sleep on a firm, flat, separate surface without pillows, loose bedding, or soft objects.
items.rationale: A safe sleep environment reduces sleep-related infant death risk.

items.title: A caregiver asks how a newborn should ride home from the hospital. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Use a correctly installed rear-facing car seat in the back seat, following manufacturer height/weight limits.
items.rationale: Rear-facing positioning protects the infant's head, neck, and spine in a crash.

items.title: A breastfeeding parent reports severe nipple pain and a clicking sound during feeds. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Observe a full feed, assess latch and infant transfer, and refer to lactation support; correct shallow latch.
items.rationale: Persistent pain and clicking suggest ineffective latch and milk transfer.

items.title: A caregiver reports giving an adult teaspoon of liquid acetaminophen to a toddler. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A caregiver reports giving an adult teaspoon of liquid acetaminophen to a toddler.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Assess exact product, concentration, dose, time, and weight; contact poison control/provider as indicated and teach oral syringe use.
items.rationale: Liquid concentrations vary; dosing must be weight-based and measured with a calibrated device.

items.title: A parent says a child missed several routine vaccines and asks to restart the entire series. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A parent says a child missed several routine vaccines and asks to restart the entire series.|response:Use the current catch-up schedule; most vaccine series do not need restarting after extended intervals.|rationale:Catch-up schedules continue valid prior doses while respecting minimum ages and intervals.
items.rationale: Catch-up schedules continue valid prior doses while respecting minimum ages and intervals.

items.title: A child with asthma uses rescue inhaler daily and wakes coughing several nights weekly. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:School asthma action plan|priority:Arrange prompt clinician review for poor control, reinforce controller adherence and spacer technique, and update written action plan.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Frequent rescue use and night symptoms indicate uncontrolled asthma and need treatment reassessment.

items.title: A client treated for food-triggered anaphylaxis is preparing for discharge. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:Anaphylaxis discharge teaching|actions:Teach epinephrine auto-injector use, carry two devices, activate emergency services after use, and arrange allergy follow-up.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Symptoms can recur after initial improvement; epinephrine is first-line and emergency evaluation is needed.

items.title: A client with diabetes has a foot ulcer probing to bone, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A client with diabetes has a foot ulcer probing to bone, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers.|priority:Obtain cultures/imaging as ordered, assess perfusion and sepsis, and prepare prolonged targeted antimicrobial and source-control plan.
items.rationale: Deep ulcer with systemic signs raises concern for bone infection requiring multidisciplinary treatment.

items.title: A client has acute hot swollen knee, fever, and severe pain with passive movement. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Septic arthritis can rapidly destroy cartilage and requires urgent drainage and antimicrobial treatment.

items.title: A client has sudden severe redness and pain at the first metatarsophalangeal joint. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Place the nursing actions in the safest priority sequence.
items.content: sequence:Recognize deterioration and assess ABCs|Escalate and obtain assistance|Implement prescribed immediate intervention|Reassess response and document
items.rationale: Acute gout is inflammatory; diagnosis and treatment must consider infection and comorbidities.

items.title: After prolonged immobilization, a client has muscle pain, dark urine, and creatine kinase 12,000 U/L. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select all findings and interventions that belong in the immediate plan of care.
items.content: answer:Notify provider, initiate prescribed isotonic fluids, monitor potassium/creatinine/urine output, and assess for compartment syndrome.|include:Focused reassessment; safety precautions; timely escalation; evaluation of response
items.rationale: Myoglobin release can cause acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia; early hydration and monitoring are important.

items.title: After chemotherapy, a client has potassium 6.2, phosphate 6.5, uric acid 11, and calcium 7.1 mg/dL. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Compare the current findings with the earlier baseline and identify deterioration and the next action.
items.content: trend:Current findings indicate possible deterioration|action:Escalate urgently, institute cardiac monitoring, administer prescribed hydration and urate-lowering therapy, and trend electrolytes/renal function.
items.rationale: Rapid tumor breakdown releases intracellular electrolytes and uric acid, risking dysrhythmia and renal failure.

items.title: A client with lung cancer develops facial/neck swelling, distended neck veins, and dyspnea worse when supine. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. Use the clinical cues to prioritize hypotheses, actions, and reassessment.
items.content: priority:Superior vena cava syndrome|actions:Elevate head, assess airway/oxygenation, notify oncology team urgently, and avoid upper-extremity venipuncture when possible.|evaluation:Venous obstruction can compromise airway and cerebral venous drainage.
items.rationale: Venous obstruction can compromise airway and cerebral venous drainage.

items.title: A client with metastatic cancer reports new severe back pain, leg weakness, and urinary retention. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Select the single best immediate nursing action.
items.content: answer:Treat as oncologic emergency, notify provider immediately, maintain spinal precautions as indicated, and prepare urgent MRI/corticosteroid/radiation evaluation.
items.rationale: New motor and sphincter deficits may signal cord compression; delay risks permanent paralysis.

items.title: A neutropenic client after chemotherapy has fever, right lower quadrant pain, and diarrhea. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Select all actions that are appropriate for the findings.
items.content: answer:Escalate urgently, keep NPO, obtain cultures/imaging as ordered, and prepare broad-spectrum antibiotics and supportive care.
items.rationale: Typhlitis can progress to perforation and sepsis in profound neutropenia.

items.title: A client with multiple myeloma has headache, blurred vision, mucosal bleeding, and confusion. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Select the four priority actions supported by the clinical findings.
items.content: answer:Notify hematology urgently, assess neurologic/visual status, and prepare for prescribed plasmapheresis.
items.rationale: Hyperviscosity impairs microcirculation and can cause neurologic, visual, and bleeding symptoms.

items.title: A client with multiple myeloma has rising creatinine and hypercalcemia. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Classify each finding as expected, concerning, or requiring immediate escalation.
items.content: finding:A client with multiple myeloma has rising creatinine and hypercalcemia.|classification:Requires focused clinical assessment|key:Monitor renal function, hydration, calcium, and nephrotoxic exposures; administer prescribed therapy and avoid dehydration.
items.rationale: Light chains, hypercalcemia, and volume depletion contribute to myeloma-associated kidney injury.

items.title: A client after stroke coughs with thin liquids and has a wet voice. The nurse is preparing a handoff and must identify the most time-sensitive concern. For each assessment cue, identify the matching nursing response and the reason.
items.content: cue:A client after stroke coughs with thin liquids and has a wet voice.|response:Keep NPO until swallow evaluation, provide oral care, and use recommended consistency and positioning after assessment.|rationale:Dysphagia increases aspiration pneumonia risk; texture modification should follow formal assessment.
items.rationale: Dysphagia increases aspiration pneumonia risk; texture modification should follow formal assessment.

items.title: An intubated client is receiving mechanical ventilation. The client is admitted to an acute-care unit; allergies and current medications are being verified. Complete the clinical statement by selecting the priority condition, action, and monitoring parameter.
items.content: condition:Ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention|priority:Maintain head-of-bed elevation when not contraindicated, oral care per protocol, daily sedation/ventilator liberation assessment, and hand hygiene.|monitoring:Reassess vital signs, clinical response, and relevant laboratory/diagnostic trends
items.rationale: Evidence-based ventilator care reduces aspiration and duration of ventilation.

items.title: A septic client has severe hypoxemia despite oxygen, bilateral opacities, and no evidence of cardiac failure. During reassessment, the nurse notes the findings have persisted despite initial comfort measures. Identify the most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:ARDS|actions:Escalate critical care, anticipate lung-protective ventilation with appropriate PEEP, and monitor oxygenation/hemodynamics.|monitor:Vital signs, oxygenation/perfusion, and condition-specific laboratory or diagnostic trends
items.rationale: ARDS causes noncardiogenic pulmonary edema; lung-protective ventilation limits ventilator-induced injury.

items.title: A mechanically ventilated client with severe ARDS remains hypoxemic despite optimized ventilation. The client has a relevant chronic condition; compare the current assessment with the documented baseline. Identify the assessment cues in the scenario that require immediate follow-up.
items.content: highlight:A mechanically ventilated client with severe ARDS remains hypoxemic despite optimized ventilation.|priority:Prepare for prolonged prone positioning by securing airway/lines, protecting pressure points, and coordinating trained team.
items.rationale: Proning can improve ventilation-perfusion matching in severe ARDS and requires meticulous safety checks.

items.title: A ventilated client is awake, hemodynamically stable, has improving cause of failure, and adequate oxygenation. The family asks what the nurse should do first while the provider is being contacted. Enter the clinically relevant threshold or measurement specified in the care protocol; verify against the client context.
items.content: answer:Use the client-specific value and protocol threshold stated in the scenario; this item requires a validated numeric key before exam use.
items.rationale: Extubation requires more than oxygenation; mental status, airway protection, and secretion burden matter.
